questions.text: What does AI stand for?

options.label: Automated Information
Artificial Intelligence
Advanced Internet
Automatic Integration

questions.text: What is machine learning?

options.label: A way to repair computers
A method where computers learn patterns from data
A programming language
A type of computer hardware

questions.text: What is data used for in machine learning?

options.label: To train and evaluate models
To increase screen brightness
To replace computer hardware
To connect a computer to Wi-Fi

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of AI?

options.label: A basic calculator performing 2 + 2
A recommendation system suggesting movies
A USB cable
A computer keyboard

questions.text: What is a machine learning model?

options.label: A physical computer
A system trained to make predictions or decisions from data
A database table
A computer monitor

questions.text: What is supervised learning?

options.label: Learning from labeled data
Learning without any data
Learning only from humans directly
Learning by changing computer hardware

questions.text: What is the purpose of training a machine learning model?

options.label: To teach the model patterns in data
To make the computer physically faster
To increase storage capacity
To install an operating system

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of supervised learning?

options.label: Grouping customers without predefined categories
Predicting house prices using labeled examples
Randomly generating numbers
Compressing a file

questions.text: What is a prediction in machine learning?

options.label: A guess or output produced by a trained model
A type of computer virus
A database backup
A programming error

questions.text: Why is it important to use good-quality data when training an AI model?

options.label: Good data can help the model make more reliable predictions
It makes the computer screen brighter
It removes the need for testing
It makes every prediction automatically correct

questions.text: What is the main difference between classification and regression in machine learning?

options.label: Classification predicts categories, while regression predicts continuous values
Classification uses no data, while regression uses data
Classification is only used for images, while regression is only used for text
Classification is always unsupervised, while regression is always supervised

questions.text: What is overfitting in machine learning?

options.label: When a model performs poorly on both training and test data
When a model learns the training data too closely and performs poorly on new data
When a model does not receive enough data to train
When a model produces exactly the same prediction every time

questions.text: Why is a dataset commonly divided into training and testing sets?

options.label: To make the dataset larger
To train the model and then evaluate how well it works on unseen data
To remove all incorrect data
To allow the model to train twice

questions.text: What does accuracy measure in a classification model?

options.label: The percentage of predictions that are correct
The number of features in the dataset
The amount of training time
The size of the neural network

questions.text: What is a feature in a machine learning dataset?

options.label: The final prediction made by the model
An input variable used by the model to make predictions
A type of machine learning algorithm
The error produced after training

questions.text: What is the purpose of a validation dataset?

options.label: To permanently store the trained model
To help tune model settings and compare model configurations during development
To replace the training dataset completely
To guarantee that the model has no errors

questions.text: What is unsupervised learning mainly used for?

options.label: Learning from data that already has correct labels
Finding patterns or groups in data without predefined labels
Testing whether a computer is connected to the internet
Manually labeling every data point

questions.text: What is clustering in machine learning?

options.label: Grouping similar data points together
Predicting a numerical value from labeled data
Removing all data from a dataset
Converting text into programming code

questions.text: Why should input features sometimes be normalized or standardized before training a model?

options.label: To ensure features with different scales are handled more appropriately by some algorithms
To remove the need for training data
To guarantee 100% prediction accuracy
To convert supervised learning into unsupervised learning

questions.text: A model has 98% accuracy on training data but only 65% accuracy on test data. What is the most likely explanation?

options.label: The model is underfitting
The model is overfitting
The model has no training data
The model is performing perfectly

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a loss function in machine learning?

options.label: To measure how different the model's predictions are from the expected results
To increase the amount of training data
To remove unnecessary features automatically
To determine how much storage the model requires

questions.text: What does gradient descent attempt to do during model training?

options.label: Increase the number of features in the dataset
Find model parameters that minimize the loss function
Remove the testing dataset
Convert an unsupervised problem into a supervised problem

questions.text: What is the learning rate in a machine learning algorithm?

options.label: The percentage of correct predictions made by the model
The amount of training data used by the model
A parameter that controls how large each optimization step is
The number of layers in a neural network

questions.text: What can happen if the learning rate is set too high?

options.label: Training may become unstable or fail to reach a good solution
The model will always achieve 100% accuracy
The dataset will automatically become larger
The model will require no training

questions.text: What is precision in a binary classification problem?

options.label: The proportion of actual positives that were correctly identified
The proportion of predicted positives that were actually positive
The proportion of all predictions that were incorrect
The total number of predictions made by the model

questions.text: What is recall designed to measure?

options.label: How many predicted positives are actually positive
How many actual positive cases the model correctly identifies
How quickly the model finishes training
How many features are used by the model

questions.text: Why can accuracy be misleading when evaluating a highly imbalanced dataset?

options.label: Accuracy cannot be calculated for classification problems
A model can achieve high accuracy by mostly predicting the majority class while performing poorly on the minority class
Accuracy only works with regression models
Accuracy always decreases when the dataset becomes larger

questions.text: What is the main purpose of regularization?

options.label: To reduce overfitting by discouraging overly complex models
To increase the number of training examples
To guarantee that all predictions are correct
To remove the need for a test dataset

questions.text: What is the bias-variance tradeoff?

options.label: The tradeoff between training speed and storage space
The balance between errors caused by overly simple assumptions and errors caused by excessive sensitivity to training data
The difference between supervised and unsupervised learning
The difference between training and testing datasets

questions.text: A model performs poorly on both its training and test datasets. Which problem is most likely occurring?

options.label: Overfitting
Underfitting
Data leakage
Class imbalance
